text:
Lian: Quick sync after the modularization RFC — I want to lock down the migration checklist for splitting the runtime hot path. Thoughts on the minimum safe contract we need?

Carlos: Minimum = request shape (headers + tenant id), stable RPC names for KV ops (GetPrefix, PutBatch, Evict) and an idempotent warm API. Anything else is negotiable.

Priya: Also include a semantic test for cache consistency across restarts. We've had subtle evictions before.

Maya: We should define owner boundaries early. Who owns lifecycle of cached entries vs who owns eviction policy?

Lian: Proposal: runtime-exec owns the physical cache and eviction algorithm. Router owns placement and tenant mapping. Router may request warms but never evict.

Carlos: Fine, but we need an adapter shim with a compatibility header so old and new code can talk during migration. Something like X-Compat-Version: 1.

Priya: +1. Add automated compatibility tests that run in CI matrix for versions 1..N, or we risk a silent break.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: test-cluster created: split-runtime-stage (image: rwinf/runtime:next-split).

Maya: Rollout plan I'd prefer: extract interface -> adapter in-tree -> co-locate on canary -> run golden e2e + perf -> flip routing for small tenant set -> range up.

Carlos: Agree. Can we quantify acceptable perf delta? I'd like a hard p99 tail budget: <= +4ms or fail gate.

Priya: Make that region-aware. APAC tends to show different tails under memory pressure.

Lian: We'll do region thresholds. I'll draft a "latency-safety" CI job that runs synthetic hot-path load.

Carlos: Also add an observability contract: every cross-facet RPC must emit a trace/span with facet_id and request_id. No black boxes.

Maya: Important for debugging. And logs for fallback routing need a sampled flag so we don't overflow logs.

Priya: For mixed-mode tenants during rollout, router must be able to map a tenant to either monolith or split. Keep mapping service tiny and eventually consistent via CDC.

Carlos: CDC caveat: if mapping lags, route to monolith fallback. Log and emit metric.

Lian: Agreed. We'll include a fallback metric and dashboard to drive rollback criteria.

infra-bot: canary-bot: canary-deploy scheduled at 1779990120.

Maya: Who's the oncall for canary? We need a runbook with probe queries and a checklist.

Lian: Volunteers: @Carlos will own adapter extraction PR, @Priya will own perf harness and thresholds, @Maya will own rollout and runbook. I'll coordinate RFC update.

Carlos: I'll land a small shim in pkg/kv/compat with a mock server and build the contract tests. Plan to open PR by Wed.

Priya: I'll spin up the perf harness using the prod-like profile (burstiness + mixed seq len). Will publish results in 5 days.

Maya: I'll author a runbook at /docs/runbooks/runtime-facet-split.md and include: prechecks, canary steps, promotion cadence (1% -> 10% -> 50%), and automatic abort rules.

Lian: Prechecks list: CI contracts green, golden-e2e pass, perf within thresholds, runbook created, canary cluster healthy.

Carlos: Add a change freeze window for the canary period to avoid noisy changes.

Priya: Also include a small bench that measures extra round trips added by the adapter in both colocated and remote modes.

Maya: For rollback: router toggles to monolith mapping, drain new pods, revert routing config, escalate if any tenant anomalies. Keep steps scripted.

Lian: We'll add a post-rollout retrospective as a required step. Even if smooth, capture remaining debt and followups.

Carlos: Security note: cross-facet RPC should carry tenant auth metadata and be authorized by execution-core. No blind accepts.

Priya: Performance note: consider colocating router-adapter pair on hot nodes first to keep <1 hop for cache access, then split once stable.

Maya: I'll incorporate region-specific memory/CPU thresholds into the rollout policy.

ops-bot: NOTE: Add a monitoring alert: facet-mismatch-errors > 0.1% for 5m -> paging.

Lian: Timeline: adapter PR by Wed, contract CI by next Tue, canary deploy after contracts pass, perf reports within 5 days of canary.

Carlos: I'll also add a small compatibility header: X-Facet-Compat: v1 and a health endpoint /_facet/health returning schema version.

Priya: One more: add an integration test where router intentionally returns fallback to verify logging and metric emission.

Maya: Sounds good. I'll post the runbook link when ready and schedule a follow-up sync after the first perf run.

Lian: Thanks everyone. If anything urgent, DM me. :thumbsup:

Carlos: ack.

Priya: ack.

Maya: ack, will ping when runbook is up.
